requirements.title: Welcome to Advance_Moonraker_Control
requirements.description:
Monitor and control Klipper printers: live dashboard, temperatures, progress, cameras, files and queues, macros, console, toolpath preview, bed mesh, energy tracking, print history, Printcast forecasts, alerts and Assist intents. Features depend on your printer and optional services. [Features and installation guide]({docs_url}).

Required: Home Assistant 2026.9 or newer, HACS 2 or newer, a working Klipper/Moonraker printer reachable from Home Assistant, and writable Home Assistant configuration storage. Home Assistant installs the pinned moonraker-api Python library and loads its built-in panel/websocket dependencies (this can happen before this wizard). Integration data is created automatically in Home Assistant storage; no SQL server, database password, AppDaemon or shell installer is required.

Optional: configure a camera for video; Spoolman on the printer for spool inventory; power, temperature and humidity entities for measurements; a notification service for alerts; an AI task provider and camera for vision; Assist/TTS/media players for voice automations. Install these separately if you want those features; HACS cannot provision printer software or arbitrary OS packages.

Accept to proceed to connection and optional-feature setup. Setup only reads printer information. Selecting a power switch later enables automatic power-off after a print and cooling. Forecasts and alerts do not guarantee print safety. HACS offers GitHub updates for your review; you choose when to install and restart.

data.accept_requirements: I understand and accept these requirements and optional features

features.title: Optional features
features.description:
Connection verified. Leave optional entities and URLs empty for a basic installation; you can change these later in Configure. Camera URLs override Moonraker webcam discovery. Install any missing sensors, notification service or AI provider through Home Assistant first. AI vision needs both a camera and an AI task entity and may send images to your chosen provider or incur charges.

Selecting a power switch enables automatic power-off after print completion, the configured delay and cooling threshold. Leave it empty to keep power under manual control. Admin-only panel access is the default; operator access permits live adjustments. Submit to create the integration, entities, sidebar panel and persistent data as it is generated.

user.title: Connect your printer
user.description: Enter the Moonraker hostname or IP, port (normally 7125), TLS setting and API key if required. Get these from your printer administrator. Enter a host without http://, https:// or a path. The connection test reads printer information and closes its temporary connection; it sends no printer commands.

init.title: Configuration

mesh_relevel.title: Bed mesh re-level recommended for {printer}
mesh_relevel.description: The measured bed mesh drifted beyond the recommended threshold compared to the stored baseline. Re-run bed leveling and clear the mesh baseline.

heater_anomaly.title: Heater anomaly detected on {printer}
heater_anomaly.description: A heater is running at full duty while its temperature falls, which usually means a detached or failing heater cartridge or thermistor. Inspect the heater before the next print.

extrusion_stall.title: Possible air printing on {printer}
extrusion_stall.description: The toolhead is moving without advancing filament for an extended period. Check for a clogged nozzle, runout, or a filament path jam.

updates_available.title: Printer component updates available for {printer}
updates_available.description: Moonraker reports pending updates for printer software components. Review them in Settings → Updates before installing.

printer_unreachable.title: {printer} is unreachable
printer_unreachable.description: The integration has not received a successful response from this Moonraker instance. Check the printer host, network path, and Moonraker service.

slow_heatup.title: Slow heat-up detected on {printer}
slow_heatup.description: A heater is taking noticeably longer than its learned baseline to reach target temperature, which suggests a degrading heater cartridge or thermistor. Inspect the heater wiring and cartridge before the next print.

spool_shortfall.title: Active spool may run out on {printer}
spool_shortfall.description: The active Spoolman spool does not hold enough filament to finish the current print. Plan a spool swap or pause the print before the filament runs out.

vision_alert.title: Possible print failure seen on {printer}
vision_alert.description: The camera check flagged likely print failure signs — spaghetti plastic, a detached part, or a bad first layer. Inspect the printer before letting the job continue.

config_changed.title: Printer configuration changed on {printer}
config_changed.description: The Klipper configuration snapshot differs from the one stored previously. Review recent printer.cfg edits if this was unexpected.

moisture_risk.title: Filament moisture risk on {printer}
moisture_risk.description: The active spool has absorbed enough humidity to threaten print quality. Dry the spool and mark it dried in the panel before starting the next job.

extrusion_drift.title: Extrusion drift detected on {printer}
extrusion_drift.description: Reported filament extrusion has drifted below this printer's learned mass baseline across recent prints, which is an early partial-clog or under-extrusion signature. Inspect the extruder and nozzle.
